subject: Evidence egress choices for audit traces
messages:
From: Alice Martin <alice@bluestone.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Evidence egress choices for audit traces

Hi Camila,

Quick question from our compliance team as we finalize the procurement packet: for audit and access traces, what are our options if we need to export records for regulatory egress (e.g., evidence package to our EU region)? Specifically:

- Can Redwood produce a time-bounded bulk export of audit/access logs for a tenant (all events) and deliver them to our S3 bucket in eu-central-1?
- What formats are available (JSONL, Parquet, compressed CSV)?
- Do you have a standard manifest and chain-of-custody we can attach to evidence?
- What are SLAs / lead times for an ad-hoc versus scheduled export, and are there any cross-border restrictions that would prevent an immediate handoff?

We also have a potential legal-hold scenario; curious what options you offer for legal-preservation vs deletion.

If easier, feel free to loop whoever owns egress on your side.

Thanks,
Alice Martin
Senior Security Manager
Bluestone Financial

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Alice Martin <alice@bluestone.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 May 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence egress choices for audit traces

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. Looping Mike from infra to cover the technical delivery and Monica from Account to capture contractual asks. High-level answers first, followed by items we need from you:

Summary (short):
- Yes, we can provide tenant-level bulk exports of audit/access traces and deliver to a customer-owned S3 bucket in eu-central-1.
- Supported formats: newline-delimited JSON (JSONL) and Parquet (row-grouped), gzip-compressed. We can also provide CSV slices on request for small windows.
- Standard evidence package: export manifest (CSV), per-file checksums (sha256), and an optional chain-of-custody template.
- Typical lead time: scheduled exports (daily/weekly) are automated; ad-hoc full-window exports (multi-GB to TB) target 48-72 hours SLA for delivery, accelerated options available on reserved capacity.
- Cross-border policy: we will not export data into a region that violates tenant residency constraints defined in the contract; for EU-resident tenants we deliver inside EU.

What we need from you to proceed on an ad-hoc:
- Tenant ID and bucket ARN (with write permissions / presigned role)
- Time window (UTC start/end) or event filters (e.g., only admin events)
- Whether you require pseudonymization/hashing of user identifiers

Attachments: I included a short PDF that lists delivery options and manifest sample. I also added a sample manifest CSV and a chain-of-custody template for review.

Next steps: Monica will follow up on contract language for the SLA; Mike and I will scope the export once you confirm tenant and window.

Best,
Camila Reyes

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
To: Alice Martin <alice@bluestone.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 May 2028 12:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence egress choices for audit traces (technical)

Hi Alice — a few technical clarifications to set expectations:

1) Export contents and sizing
- Audit/access traces include timestamp, event_type, tenant_id, actor_id (we can hash), resource_id, ip, geo, and request/response metadata. For very large windows we chunk by day and produce multiple Parquet files (row-grouped for fast query). Expect ~500–900 MB/day for a high-activity tenant; exact numbers vary.

2) Delivery and integrity
- We deliver via either: (a) Redwood pushes to your S3 bucket using a short-lived presigned PUT role, or (b) customer pulls from an authenticated HTTPS staging URL. All files are sha256-signed and we include a manifest with per-file checksum + total byte count.

3) Residency & legal hold
- For tenants flagged as EU-resident, exports are executed in our EU region and data never crosses out. For legal-hold we can: (a) freeze deletion for a specified window (we mark data as preserved in our index), and (b) provide a locked export snapshot. Freezing is supported as part of an Enterprise add-on; we need DPA / SOW language.

4) Redaction/pseudonymization
- We can apply deterministic hashing (sha256 with salt) to actor identifiers before export. Note: hashing prevents reversible identification but does not remove attributes like IP that may be considered personal data. We can apply IP truncation on request.

5) Performance SLA & accelerated path
- Standard ad-hoc: 48–72 hours. Accelerated (paid): 12–24 hours; requires dedicated export worker capacity — usually scoped under Dedicated or as a one-off professional service.

If you want, I can provide a short sample Parquet + manifest for a 30-day window so your legal/compliance can inspect.

–Mike
Michael Grant
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Camila and Mike — this is very helpful. A couple of follow-ups from our side:

- We are EU-resident; please ensure export is executed in EU and delivered to our eu-central-1 bucket (ARN: arn:aws:s3:::bluestone-eu-audit-archive).
- For the legal-hold scenario, we need an SLA that guarantees snapshot delivery within 5 business days and an option to extend preservation for up to 2 years; can you confirm if that fits under an Enterprise add-on?
- Please send the sample Parquet + manifest for a 30-day window and the chain-of-custody template so our legal can review.

Also: we prefer hashed actor_ids with a customer-supplied salt if possible (we can provide). Can you confirm IP truncation as an option?

Finally, we'll need a DocuSign for the SOW changes — feel free to attach the SOW link.

Best,
Alice

3) Technical choices
- We'll produce Parquet + manifest (sha256 per-file). Mike will prepare a sample for a 30-day window and will apply deterministic hashing to actor_id using your salt; IP truncation is supported (we'll truncate to /24 by default unless you request otherwise).

4) Immediate asks for you
